Well, here's something new for you. This is Paginini Caprici 5 but it's not played on a Martin. This is played on a delightful Taylor classical guitar. I'm going to skip giving you the model number 'cause then you'd be able to look it up and see the price. Yeah... I paid more for this guitar than I've paid for quite a few different cars.

You guitarists might notice a strange sound about it. It's actually strung with steel and nylon. I'm using a very light gauge steel on EADG and my BE are both nylon. I don't normally buy "sets" of strings - most of the time. I try to buy multiple gauges and keep them all organized in totes with labels. If I am buying sets, instead of boxes of individual strings, I tend to buy them in bulk.

Tip: Your local music store will almost certainly give you a discount if you buy stuff in bulk. (There's more...) I buy strings and picks in bulk - ordering whole cases. It's actually not expensive and you can build your collection up slowly.

But - bonus tip: Shop at the same music store and get to know the people there. They almost certainly have a "musician discount." Even if you're not in a performing band, they'll still give you the musician's discount. Don't use the big chain shops, they're garbage and their employees don't know a damned thing. Find the one that's off the beaten path.

I'll throw a plug in for my local shop - they're Everyday Music, located in Farmington, Maine. I sometimes use Down Home which is over in Fairfield. In both cases, I know the owners and I actually go to them for different stuff. My guitar stuff I get almost exclusively at one, and anything percussion related (and sometimes pedals) I get at the other. Even though I seldom drum, both stores can count on me stopping in twice a year. In the Everyday Music case, they can count on me stopping in once every two months, sometimes more often. I call ahead and order stuff, instead of spending my money online.

I do, however, sometimes make larger purchases from Musician's Friend. Mics, mic stands, and amps? They're a great place - and they have sooooo many pedals!
